bangor-me 1f5d0e5000b1.meeting: Advisory Committee on Racial Equity, Inclusion, and Human Rights, 2026-10-06

shown.headline: Committee continues discussion on training recommendations for Code of Ethics §33-5.1 and community engagement.
shown.summary: The committee will continue discussing recommendations for training related to Code of Ethics §33-5.1, following a City Council referral. It will also discuss community engagement.

The Council heard public comments on homelessness, opioid funding, and the 103 Main Street property, then acted on routine items and new business. It postponed a vote on accepting MaineHousing funds for Project HOPE, gave first readings to several ordinances and resolves including a data center moratorium and a bond for land at 103 Maine Avenue, and approved three special amusement permits.

shown.headline: License Board to discuss Mikado Asian Cuisine alcohol license status and a new liquor license application for Amnol Market at 268-272 Rantoul Street.
shown.summary: The board will review the status of the all-alcoholic beverages license from the former Mikado Asian Cuisine and hear from Deep Saini, LLC dba Amnol Market about a new Off-Premise Chapter 15 Green Grocery License. The board will also discuss a compliance check at JK Harrigan's dba Harrigan's Cork 'N Cask and review several one-day license applications.

shown.headline: Approved May 20, 2026 minutes and reviewed harbor financial and operational updates.
shown.summary: The board approved the May 20, 2026 minutes 6-0. The capital fund grew to $870,700, and kayak rack revenue reached 106% of budget due to higher occupancy. The harbormaster reported on debris removal, mooring field issues, bridge construction work, and the Lobster Rocks marker, and noted Beverly Main Streets will continue as an all-volunteer organization.

shown.headline: Held three security deposit hearings on Buell Street and Hyde Street properties; board deliberated privately after adjourning.
shown.summary: The board held hearings on three security deposit cases: 108 Buell Street, 21 Hyde Street Unit 3, and 21 Hyde Street Unit 1. Parties presented evidence and testimony in each case, and the hearings were closed. The board then deliberated in private after the meeting adjourned.

shown.headline: Referred Chapter 26 Industrial Pollution Prevention Program ordinance to City Council for adoption; approved plan to increase e-bike and e-moto enforcement and education.
shown.summary: The committee reviewed updates to the Chapter 26 Industrial Pollution Prevention Program ordinance and voted to send it to the full City Council for a second reading with a recommendation to adopt it. The committee also discussed problems with e-bikes and e-motos, including safety concerns raised by a resident and police observations, and voted to direct BPD, DPW, Parks, and the City Attorney's Office to pursue signage, enforcement, and outreach to schools, South Burlington, and the Vermont DMV.

shown.headline: Design Advisory Board meeting canceled for October 13, 2026.
shown.summary: The Design Advisory Board meeting scheduled for this date has been canceled. No business will be conducted.

shown.headline: Approved minutes, reelected board officers, and reviewed draft vegetation ordinance
shown.summary: The board approved prior meeting minutes and reelected its current slate of officers for another year. Members discussed plans for a Conservation Board retreat, an ecosystem services analysis funding request, and gave detailed feedback on a draft amended vegetation ordinance.

shown.headline: Review of 2027 grant applications, grant completion reports, and updates on current grant applications.
shown.summary: The council will review pending 2027 grant applications, discuss preliminary rejections and acceptances, and go over panel books. It will also cover updates and completion reports on current grant applications.

shown.headline: Building & Finance Subcommittee reviews DPW tickets, FY25 audit, special education costs, and budget transfers.
shown.summary: The subcommittee will hear a Chief Financial Officer's report and discuss DPW tickets, the FY25 end of year report audit, special education out-of-district tuition and transportation, staffing, budget transfers, content planning, and GHS library technical issues.

shown.headline: Recommended National Grid pole on Bellevue Avenue, preservation restrictions for Haskell House and Temple-Hayden Cottage, and withdrawal of 187 Atlantic Ave soil permit
shown.summary: The Planning & Development Committee recommended the City Council approve a National Grid petition to install a new utility pole near 17 Conant Avenue, approve preservation restriction agreements for the Haskell House at 11 Lincoln Street and the Temple-Hayden Cottage at 62, 62R, 64, and 66 Eastern Point Boulevard, and accept the withdrawal of a soil removal permit application from 187 Atlantic Ave Holdings, LLC. Several other zoning matters were continued to future meetings.

shown.headline: Approval of Superintendent's goals, student handbooks, prior year expenses of $51,317.23, and acceptance of two grants.
shown.summary: The meeting will cover the Superintendent's Report, a school opening update, and student handbooks. The Committee will also act on the Superintendent's Goals, Student Handbooks, prior year expenses totaling $51,317.23, and grant acceptances including a $423,733 preschool grant and a $40,000 civics grant.

shown.headline: New Common VIC licenses for Los Compadres Restaurant and El Piloncito Supermarket, plus a complaint against Eleven Kitchen & Bar.
shown.summary: The board will review two new Common VIC license applications, hear a complaint about Eleven Kitchen & Bar regarding ownership, management, and liquor license and outdoor dining, and consider a tabled liquor license transfer for Father & Son DBA Envy Lounge.

shown.headline: Declined to sell cemetery land to a Warwick Street abutter and approved sending a Memorial Day letter to local officials.
shown.summary: The board discussed the Superintendent's report on Christmas ornament inventory, a request from a Warwick Street neighbor to buy cemetery land, and concerns about revenue splits with the city. It voted to send a letter about Memorial Day arrangements to several officials and voted to draft a letter to the Acting Community Development Director declining to sell cemetery land to any abutters. Discussions on financial accounting, FEMA funds, a horse-drawn hearse donation, and street signage ended without a vote.

shown.headline: Council approved first passage of mobile home park rent moratorium ordinance 5-2, but failed to waive rules for final passage.
shown.summary: The Council held a public hearing on extending a moratorium ordinance on rent increases for mobile home park lots, effective September 29, 2026. Many residents and park owners spoke for and against the extension. The Council approved first passage of the ordinance by a 5-2 roll call vote, but a motion to waive council rules to allow final passage the same night did not pass, so the final passage motion was not brought forward.

shown.headline: Lewiston School Committee reviewed personnel hires, transfers, resignations, and retirements on a consent agenda; no public input was given.
shown.summary: The committee reviewed a consent agenda listing new hires, transfers, resignations, and one retirement for certified staff, coaches, educational technicians, management, and support employees across district schools. No public input was offered, and the meeting adjourned.

shown.headline: Personnel-only consent agenda and public input session.
shown.summary: The School Committee will act on a personnel item on the consent agenda and take public input on school and educational matters.

shown.headline: Granted Certificate of Appropriateness for exterior renovations at 192 Bates Street, 6-0.
shown.summary: The board reviewed an application for a Certificate of Appropriateness for exterior renovations at 192 Bates Street and approved it 6-0. The board also discussed plans for the upcoming HBRB Awards Ceremony on August 6, 2026, and approved the June 4, 2026 minutes 6-0.

shown.headline: Discussion of ordinance amending Chapter 176, "Housing Standards".
shown.summary: The subcommittee will discuss a proposed ordinance change to Chapter 176, titled "Housing Standards".

shown.summary: The Board of Parks reviewed requests for park and field use permits from many residents, churches, and youth sports leagues, approving most with fees, waivers, or fee reductions by or votes. Several cricket league permit requests and two flag football field requests were held over or carried to the next meeting, and five items were declined because no one appeared to represent them.

shown.headline: Approved new member appointments, retirement applications, withdrawals/transfers, Superannuation for James Connolly, and a Medical Panel for Stephen Prince.
shown.summary: The board accepted April meeting minutes, warrants, payrolls, new member appointments, retirement applications, and withdrawals/transfers, all with all present in favor. In executive session, the board discussed ADR applications for James Connolly, Frederick Wilson, and Stephen Prince, then approved Superannuation for James Connolly ahead of his ADR application and approved a Medical Panel request for Stephen Prince. The board also approved closing the office early on May 27, 2026, so staff could attend Domenic Fermano's wake.

shown.headline: Approved Nan McKay contract piggyback for Mexico, Missouri, trash bag price increase to $73.16 per case, and $6,131.82 in tenant balance write-offs.
shown.summary: The board approved letting the Housing Authority of the City of Mexico, Missouri use MHA's Nan McKay task order contract. It also approved an amended contract amount, a trash bag price increase from WASTEZERO, and two additional tenant balance write-offs totaling $6,131.82.

malden-ma 0d56f35640f0.meeting: Commission on Climate Action and Sustainability, 2026-10-14

shown.headline: Commission to review and score applications for the Youth Climate Action Fund (YCAF).
shown.summary: The commission will go over the YCAF application guidelines and scoring rubric, then read and score submitted applications before discussing them as a group. It will also plan its next meeting agenda.

malden-ma 904edb2ed399.meeting: Municipal Building Committee - Malden River Works, 2026-09-03

shown.headline: Approved August 6 minutes and designLAB invoice for $38,430 while discussing pile cost increase of about $31,000
shown.summary: The committee approved the 8/6/26 meeting minutes and reviewed project updates on the boathouse equipment racks, pile foundation cost changes, and project financing. The committee approved designLAB invoice 26-02.0726 for construction documents billing. The team discussed switching to timber piles after structural engineers found a miscalculation in pile load requirements.

shown.headline: Approved a revised Canal Street mural design and amended Stark Brewing's outdoor dining hours in Arms Lot.
shown.summary: The committee discussed and approved a revised mural design from Manchester Connects for the Canal Street and Pleasant Street crossing, then voted to expedite that report to the Board. It also discussed and approved changes to Stark Brewing's outdoor dining agreement for Arms Lot, adjusting the days and hours allowed, including Friday, July 3. A request from 784 Corning Road LLC to purchase land at 784 Corning Road remained tabled.

shown.headline: Annual vote on executive officers, followed by chair, treasurer, real estate, and marketing committee reports.
shown.summary: The agenda covers the yearly vote on executive officers, then reports from the Chair, Treasurer, Strategic Initiatives/Real Estate, and Marketing/Communications committees, plus an update from the Manchester Economic Development Office.

shown.headline: Special permit applications for a Walmart warehouse at 256 Pleasant St. and a garage addition at 11 Tobey Ave.
shown.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals will consider a special permit for a proposed warehouse use at 256 Pleasant St. (Walmart) and a special permit for a 2 car garage addition at 11 Tobey Ave. The board will also accept the 2027 meeting schedule.

shown.headline: Recommended final passage of budget transfers for road funding, hydrant fees, and salary negotiations
shown.summary: The committee recommended increasing the annual motor vehicle permit fee funding for road and highway expenditures from $1,000,000 to $2,000,000. It also recommended transfers of $85,100 to cover increased hydrant fees and $10,500 for salary negotiations. Public comment raised questions about a $76,000 street lighting budget transfer.

shown.headline: Public hearings on variance requests for 48 Buckmeadow Road and 20 Canal Street properties.
shown.summary: The board will hear a variance request from Miguel Bisono for 48 Buckmeadow Road covering land area, open space, number of structures, and driveway width. It will also hear a variance request from Anand Mahendrakar for 20 Canal Street covering minimum land area.

shown.headline: Human Affairs Committee heard presentation from Revive Recovery Resource Center on recovery housing and support services.
shown.summary: Revive Recovery Resource Center Executive Director Jessica Carter presented to the committee on recovery housing and the organization's services in the Nashua area. No new business, resolutions, or ordinances were taken up, and the committee adjourned after the presentation and public comment.
The Board voted 6-0 to grant the Conditional Use for a period of three years.

shown.headline: Votes on Roux Institute Brownfields grant amendment, Job Creation Grant Program guidelines, grant applications, and loans for Garden Concerts, LLC (Portland House of Music), 25 Temple Street.
shown.summary: The board will review a Brownfields grant amendment request from Roux Institute and vote on changes to the Job Creation Grant Program Guidelines. It will also vote on job creation grant applications, PDC Award Event nominations, and a commercial loan plus interest-free storefront loan for Garden Concerts, LLC (Portland House of Music), 25 Temple Street.

shown.headline: Council passed a rent control resolution 7-2, appropriated $386,037 for Hope House rehabilitation, approved several grants, and amended Fore Street traffic rules.
shown.summary: The council approved appointments to the Casco Bay Trail Board, outdoor dining for Terlingua LLC, and an EMS Transport Plan. It passed an amended resolution on rent control and tenant protections 7-2 after extensive public comment, approved $386,037 for Hope House rehabilitation, a MaineDOT intersection agreement, several grants including $73,721, $20,000, and $151,500, an opioid settlement funds code amendment, and a Fore Street traffic schedule change. Two EPA Brownfields funding orders of $500,000 and $1,000,000 received only a first reading.

shown.headline: Economic Development Commission to discuss Lofts at Fairgrounds and South County Commons District 5 Apartments preliminary plans, plus URI medical school and SMART Committee work.
shown.summary: The commission will review preliminary plan applications for Lofts at Fairgrounds and South County Commons District 5 Apartments. Members will also discuss the Old Tower Hill Road Neighborhood Plan, a future URI medical school, resuming SMART Committee statistical work, and collaboration with other town boards.

shown.headline: Approved June 4, 2026 minutes and raised no objection to a CRMC swim float application at 257 Walmsley Ln.
shown.summary: The Waterfront Advisory Commission reviewed old business including the Harbor Management Plan, GIS mapping of shoreline access, boat storage rights-of-way, hydrilla treatment, and the Narrow River boat ramp project. The commission approved prior meeting minutes and voted not to object to a CRMC swim float application at 257 Walmsley Ln.

shown.headline: Operations Committee to review financial reports, cafeteria reports, and maintenance/facilities project updates.
shown.summary: The meeting covers the district's financial report including the 2% Fund and Fiscal Year 2026-2027 transfer request, cafeteria operation reports, and an update on maintenance and facilities projects.

wallingford-ct 07023be857df.meeting: Quinnipiac River Linear Trail Advisory Committee, 2026-11-05

shown.summary: The committee will hear a Town Engineer report and updates from its Financial, Grants/Applications, Publicity/Social Media, Signage, and Trail Expansion subcommittees. The meeting also includes a public question and answer period and other business.

shown.headline: Executive session on Assistant Principal candidate, resignations, and Business Manager's contract.
shown.summary: The board will meet in executive session to discuss candidates for Assistant Principal at Moran Middle School, review resignation acceptances, and discuss the Business Manager's contract. Following the executive session, the board may take action on these three items.

shown.headline: Reviewed treasurer's report showing budget surplus and discussed volunteer tasks for upcoming events.
shown.summary: Treasurer Larry Russo reported the committee's budget of $32,215 plus $2,00 from the Probate budget was approved by the Town Council, with total expenditures of $28,949.06 leaving a surplus of $5,264 to return to the town. Members reviewed a list of tasks for upcoming events, including Halloween on October 23rd and Seasons of Celebration on December 5th, and discussed finding volunteers.

shown.headline: Approved $678,550 Teamsters contract funding, $1,158,400 non-union pay raise, Pelham Road easements, and several street resurfacing projects; denied 1432 Main Street rezoning.
shown.summary: The council held public hearings on special permits for 220 Moody Street and 96 Tower Road, continuing both to October dates, and approved a street opening permit for Nicholas DiDuca at 20 Gale Street. It approved funding for a Teamsters union contract, a non-union employee pay raise, infrastructure and equipment purchases, two Pelham Road easements, and resurfacing on several streets. It also approved naming part of 617 Lexington Street for Robert Eagle, denied renaming it for John Daddona, denied a zoning change at 1432 Main Street, and withdrew a zoning amendment at 181-185 Felton Street.

shown.headline: Tabled equity plan vote, adopted AI guidelines, approved consent agenda and out-of-district requests
shown.summary: The Waltham School Committee met in executive session on collective bargaining and litigation matters, then held a regular meeting covering curriculum updates, an equity plan presentation, and an AI guidance policy. The Committee approved the consent agenda, staff out-of-district requests, AI guidelines, and bills on the warrant, while tabling a vote on the three-year equity plan until September 2, 2026.

shown.headline: Executive session on negotiations with nonunion personnel for the Assistant Superintendent for Finance and Operations position.
shown.summary: The School Committee will meet in executive session to discuss strategy for and conduct negotiations with nonunion personnel regarding the Assistant Superintendent for Finance and Operations.
